observations.population: 820 major-party candidates in contested state lower-house races across 18 states, 2008
observations.caveat: Selected group means, not a universal office-level weekly schedule; survey response rate 34.4 percent before the contested-race subset.

observations.value: A majority of non-incumbent men in this survey worked full time during the election; a majority of women in all three experience groups worked less than full time.
observations.caveat: Association in one sample, not a rule by gender or a mandate to stop working.

observations.metric: NYC matching-funds program City Council spending limit, USD
observations.population: Participating 2025 New York City Council campaigns
observations.caveat: Legal cap for program participants, not actual spending or a national local-race benchmark.

observations.population: 2025 New York City election cycle, all campaigns and mayoral subset
observations.caveat: Aggregate, not per-candidate. City Council public funds totaled $18.6 million; independent council spending is separate.

observations.population: 244,401 individual contributions to 2025 NYC campaigns across offices
observations.caveat: Donation size, not campaign spending; not a city council-only statistic.

observations.metric: filing fee and petition signature requirements in the existing game corpus
observations.caveat: The current game marks fees and petitions not established; do not substitute a national fee or treat unknown as zero.

observations.metric: paid campaign staff counts in a surveyed state and local candidate pool
observations.population: 2024 state and local candidates recruited through Pipeline Fund partner organizations and BallotReady
observations.caveat: Unweighted, partner-sourced respondent pool; not nationally representative and not broken out by individual office. These percentages do not set a staffing distribution for every city, county, or state race.

observations.metric: reported volunteer mobilization help needed versus received
observations.population: Same 2024 Pipeline Fund state and local candidate respondent pool
observations.caveat: Perceived support need and receipt, not volunteer counts or a probability that a campaign receives a volunteer.

observations.metric: candidate work and income tradeoffs while campaigning
observations.population: Same 2024 Pipeline Fund state and local candidate respondent pool
observations.caveat: Self-reported outcomes in a nonrepresentative sample; no universal quit-job rule or salary loss amount.

observations.metric: retail postage for one domestic one-ounce letter, USD per piece
observations.population: USPS retail domestic one-ounce letters in 2024
observations.caveat: Postage only, not design, printing, list acquisition, labor, or bulk political mail pricing. This is a time-bound unit price, not the total cost of a campaign mailer.

costDrivers.caveat: Official federal expenditure categories, not prices.

phasePattern.preCampaign: Build plan, donor and voter lists, budget, volunteer capacity, and issue positions before intensive field work.
phasePattern.campaign: Combine direct voter contact, fundraising, public events, and media; allocate candidate hours against outside work and governing duties.
phasePattern.finalDays: Shift capacity toward targeted persuasion, supporter contact, and election-day turnout work.
phasePattern.caveat: Qualitative planning pattern from an international training example. No fixed U.S. phase length or universal weekly schedule is established.

federalCandidateCommittee: candidate personal funds and reportable loans
individual contributions, including family subject to applicable limits
fundingChannels.localExample: New York City's 2025 matching-funds program supplied public funds to participating candidates; this is not universal to local elections.
fundingChannels.caveat: Independent expenditures by outside committees are not cash handed to the candidate campaign. Limits, eligibility, reporting, and public financing vary by office, election cycle, and jurisdiction.

gameplayCalibration.reason: Action durations, prices, contact probabilities, and electoral effects need separate design choices tied to office, geography, capacity, and phase. The observations above are samples and cannot be copied into every race.
